title: Field instrument service history
background: A fictional laboratory consortium links service events to the same physical measurement instrument. Serial text is only meaningful together with the manufacturer namespace; parts can be exchanged without making two instruments the same.
observations: The store maintains a union structure of accepted matches and a latest-value summary. An update handler receives both event time and ingestion time but currently chooses the last arrival.
Messages can be repeated or arrive late. A service-center correction withdraws an earlier serial observation; the resulting deletion event can arrive before the original event is replayed.
An imported workshop bundle includes a common loaner contact and can connect instruments previously kept separate. Some source observations must be purged under an authorized retention request.

The engineering proposal is to remove the deleted source row and leave existing cluster IDs and summaries untouched. A periodic rebuild from active observations is also feasible, but its cost has not been estimated.
constraints: Downstream calibration notices use stable public instrument IDs. Incorrect notices and resurrected purged data are unacceptable.
Only design work is authorized. Required deletion semantics and retained audit metadata need approval from the responsible data owner.
request: Compare maintenance designs and propose a bounded replay and deletion acceptance plan covering externally visible behavior, operational cost, and unresolved authorization questions.
